title: ollama/ollama — Get up and running with Kimi, GLM, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Qwen, Gemma and other models.
content:
Start building with open models.
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | shirm https://ollama.com/install.ps1 | iexcurl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
The official Ollama Docker image ollama/ollama is available on Docker Hub.
ollama
You'll be prompted to run a model or connect Ollama to your existing agents or applications such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode , Codex, Copilot,  and more.
To launch a specific integration:
ollama launch claude
Supported integrations include Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, DeepSeek Harness, Droid, and OpenCode.
Use OpenClaw to turn Ollama into a personal AI assistant across WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, and more:
ollama launch openclaw
Run and chat with Gemma 4:
ollama run gemma4
See ollama.com/library for the full list.
See the quickstart guide for more details.
Ollama has a REST API for running and managing models.
curl http://localhost:11434/api/chat -d '{
  "model": "gemma4",
  "messages": [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": "Why is the sky blue?"
  }],
  "stream": false
}'
See the API documentation for all endpoints.
pip install ollama
from ollama import chat
response = chat(model='gemma4', messages=[
  {
    'role': 'user',
    'content': 'Why is the sky blue?',
  },
])
print(response.message.content)npm i ollama
import ollama from "ollama";
const response = await ollama.chat({
  model: "gemma4",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Why is the sky blue?" }],
});
console.log(response.message.content);

report.summary: Ollama's README documents running open models like Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen and Gemma locally via one-line installs, a REST API and SDKs.
report.background: For years, running a capable LLM meant either paying per-token for a cloud API or wrestling with Python environments, CUDA versions and model weights by hand. That changed with llama.cpp, Georgi Gerganov's C/C++ inference engine that made quantized models run efficiently on consumer CPUs and GPUs. Ollama built on that lineage, packaging a model runner, a library of pre-quantized weights and a simple CLI so that 'ollama run <model>' replaced pages of setup. The result is a local-first ecosystem: developers keep prompts, code and data on their own machines, avoid API bills and rate limits, and can still reach frontier-class open weights — DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, gpt-oss and Gemma — within minutes of release. As open models close the gap with closed ones, tooling like Ollama has become the default on-ramp for private, offline and cost-controlled AI.
key_points: One-command install and run: a single curl or PowerShell script installs Ollama, and 'ollama run gemma4' downloads and starts a chat. The model library at ollama.com/library lists all supported open models, so trying a new release requires no Python, CUDA or Docker knowledge.

Agent integrations are now first-class: 'ollama launch claude', Codex, Copilot CLI, Droid and OpenCode let local models plug into existing coding agents, while OpenClaw turns Ollama into a personal assistant reachable through WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and Discord.

Programmatic access is simple: a REST API on localhost:11434 handles chat and model management, with official Python and JavaScript SDKs (pip install ollama, npm i ollama) that mirror the same chat/messages interface used by OpenAI-style clients.

A huge third-party ecosystem has formed around it: hundreds of listed projects span chat UIs (Open WebUI, LibreChat, Lobe Chat), RAG engines (RAGFlow, AnythingLLM), IDE assistants (Continue, Cline, Void), agents (AutoGPT, crewAI) and SDKs for .NET, Java, Rust, Swift, Go, Ruby, PHP, R and Julia.

The project serves as a neutral compatibility layer: by exposing a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint and supporting a wide SDK matrix, it lets developers swap between local open weights and cloud providers without rewriting application code.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Ollama cements local inference as a mainstream deployment target rather than a hobbyist niche, pressuring closed API vendors on price and privacy and giving open-weight labs a distribution channel the day they publish. For developers, it removes infrastructure friction: prototyping against DeepSeek, Qwen or Gemma locally, then moving to cloud only when scale demands it, with the same chat-style API either way. For regular users, it means private assistants that work offline, without subscriptions or data leaving the machine — increasingly viable as open models approach frontier quality. The main risks are hardware limits on consumer machines, weaker performance than top cloud models on hard tasks, and a fragmented ecosystem of overlapping front-ends.
report.tools: Start with Ollama itself, then pick a front-end: Open WebUI or LibreChat for a ChatGPT-like interface, AnythingLLM or RAGFlow for document Q&A, and Continue or Cline inside VS Code for coding. For plumbing, LiteLLM unifies providers, LangChain and LlamaIndex handle orchestration, OpenLIT or Opik adds monitoring, and Ollama Fortress secures exposed instances. Check ollama.com/library for current model tags before downloading.
